newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch grocers combine targets 10 pct EPS growth.
newsitem.headline: Dutch grocers combine targets 10 pct EPS growth.

text.p: Dutch supermarket chains De Boer Winkelbedrijven and unlisted Unigro said on Wednesday they expected their planned merger to generate double-digit earnings per share growth.
"We are targeting earnings per share growth of at least 10 percent a year," Unigro chairman Robert ter Haar told a news conference.
He said that during the first full merger year the new combine would post proforma net earnings of 90 million guilders.
"We expect a fundamental improvement in the valuation of the shares (compared to De Boer's current valuation)," he added.
"De Boer Unigro will be a growth stock," he stressed.
Last year De Boer posted net profits of 33.2 million guilders on turnover of 1.7 billion guilders.
Unigro net profit for the 1995/96 fiscal year ended January 31 amounted to 25.2 million guilders.

But Unigro's finance director Wouter Kranenberg said net earnings would have been almost twice as high if the company had followed customary Dutch accounting practice of booking goodwill against shareholders' equity.
"Previously Unigro has channeled goodwill payments for acquisitions through its profit and loss account -- naturally this depresses the bottom line," he said.
Instead it would now write down goodwill against shareholders' equity.
"Last year this would have resulted in a virtual doubling of the net profit -- that is to some 50 million guilders," Kranenberg said.
